title: When you land
body:
Andorra has no airport and no train station — everyone arrives overland by road, almost always on the Direct Bus coach from Barcelona–El Prat airport (T1/T2) to the Andorra la Vella bus station. Buses run 365 days a year, about every 2 hours, first departure 07:30 (T1) / 07:45 (T2), last at 23:00/23:15, and the ride is ≈3.5 hours.

The bus terminates at the Estació Nacional d'Autobusos on Avinguda de Tarragona, a 5–10 minute walk into the Barri Antic (old quarter) where most mid-range hotels sit. Book online in advance at andorradirectbus.es — arrive 30 minutes before departure for the return leg to the airport.
checklist: Book the Barcelona airport ↔ Andorra la Vella Direct Bus both ways before you fly
Keep the return bus at least 4.5 hours before your flight (3.5h ride + 30 min buffer + airport time)
Pack for cold: Andorra la Vella averages 7°C/-2°C in early November, with regular light snow at altitude

title: Local essentials
body:
Andorra uses the euro despite not being an EU member — a special monetary agreement with the EU lets it mint its own coins. Cards and contactless are accepted almost everywhere; ATMs are common in Andorra la Vella and mostly fee-free on withdrawal (your own bank's foreign-transaction fee may still apply).

The official language is Catalan, but Spanish is the most widely understood second language, with French and Portuguese also common — English is patchy outside hotels and the busiest shops.

Mobile roaming is not EU-regulated here, so a European or US carrier plan can get expensive fast; buying a local Andorra Telecom prepaid SIM or a dedicated eSIM before or on arrival is the usual fix.

title: Entry & documents
body:
US passport holders don't need an Andorran visa and can stay up to 90 days. Because Andorra is outside the Schengen area but only reachable through Spain or France (both Schengen members), it's the Schengen entry rule that actually governs the trip: your passport must be valid at least 3 months past your planned departure from the Schengen area, and issued within the last 10 years.

Carry proof of onward travel and accommodation — standard Schengen border-check documents — since the physical border crossing happens on the France/Spain side, not inside Andorra.

title: Phone & data
body: Andorra sits outside the EU roaming umbrella, so a US or EU home plan can bill at expensive out-of-bundle rates here. An eSIM activated for arrival, or a local Andorra Telecom prepaid SIM bought in Andorra la Vella, is the standard workaround — 4G coverage is solid across the compact territory, including on the hiking routes near town.

title: Booking checklist
checklist: Flights into Barcelona–El Prat (BCN) — the standard gateway for the airport bus
Direct Bus tickets, both directions, at andorradirectbus.es
Accommodation in or near the Barri Antic, Andorra la Vella
Travel insurance — the EHIC does not cover Andorra, and uninsured emergency care bills the full cost
Dinner reservation at Borda Estevet for at least one night — seating is limited and demand is high
Caldea thermal spa tickets online in advance, especially for a Saturday visit
